newsitem.title: USA: Delicate surgery performed on girl mauled by bear.
newsitem.headline: Delicate surgery performed on girl mauled by bear.

text.p: A teenaged girl mauled by a bear while camping in Arizona last summer underwent a rare nerve transplant Tuesday in surgery designed to save her right leg.
Washington University School of Medicine said the procedure on Anna Knochel began at 7:30 a.m. local time and was expected to last from eight to 14 hours.

It was performed by Susan Mackinnon, a reconstructive surgeon at the medical school who is believed to be the only surgeon in the world who has done such nerve transplants, school spokeswoman Mary Carollo said.

Tuesday's surgery is only the seventh time Mackinnon has performed the operation since she developed the technique in 1989. In it the girl's sciatic nerve, running down the back of the leg, is being replaced with portions of two nerves from human cadavers.

Carollo said Knochel might lose the limb by amputation without the surgery. The girl, who lives in Tucson, Ariz., was attacked by a black bear July 25 in her sleep while she was a counsellor on a camping trip on Mount Lemmon.
